title: Joe Jordan and the union agent Peek-a-boo Jimmy
summary: Thomas explains the union agent Peek-a-boo Jimmy, who tried to stop out-of-town musicians from working in New York, and starts to describe Joe Jordan.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Yeah, well, that's what he's got, '34 with Henderson Tapps' for a few months and then with Ferman Pat band at Small____.
Ferman Tapps, yes. Well, a fellow by the name of Joe Jordan, he passed about a couple years ago. He was about 80 or 90 years old.
He was a trumpet player, wasn't he?
No, I think Joe played piano. And we did some things around town and somehow I happened to run into Joe Jordan. Don't let me leave out Peek-a-boo Jimmy. Please don't leave him out.
Yeah, well, how does he come in the picture?
Well, he enters the picture this way because you know me and him, he'll knock you out. You know that's an agent. That's his interpretation, not to unionize.

He doesn't want you to work. The union says you can't work, according to Peek-a-boo Jimmy so you're not going to work in this town because Peek-a-boo's union says you're not going to work in this town. And he's a husky cat, you know. And if you want to get past him, you're going to have a helluva fight so I say, let's have the fight. (?) with Henderson so we made a deal about it ...
But when you say he was an agent, in what way?
Oh, he was a union agent. Oh, I see. So, you'd have to sort of get around him?
Oh, you've got to get around him, you know. If you can't, you know. But he was a very kindly guy. He had to do
his job as it was reported to him. That's all.
